ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: People's Republic of China Anti-Money Laundering Law (as amended); PBOC/SAMR Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information Registration of Market Entities (Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (as amended); Taiwan Regulations Governing Customer Due Diligence and Record-Keeping for Financial Institutions and Designated Non-Financial Businesses; and the Taiwan Ministry of Justice Anti-Money Laundering Bureau implementing guidelines.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Legal Existence Extract) of the PRC parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), local municipal market regulation bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Taiwan is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so a Hague Apostille is prohibited and will not be accepted. Use the exclusive non-Hague Cross-Strait Consular Legalization channel: (1) notarize the instrument at a PRC notary public; (2) transmit the notarial certificate through the provincial notary association to the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) in Taipei; (3) obtain SEF verification before filing with the Taiwan registry and bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Legal Existence Report from the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille is not available because Taiwan is not an Apostille party; complete the same Cross-Strait Consular Legalization route: PRC notarization, provincial notary association transmission to SEF, SEF verification, then use the verified extract for Taiwan company registration and bank KYC.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney authorizing the Taiwan WFOE formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors / shareholders' meeting of the PRC parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille path exists for Taiwan; notarize the signed resolution and signatory authority at a PRC notary office, forward through the provincial notary association to SEF for authentication, and present the SEF-verified copy to the Taiwan registry and bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of Association of the PRC parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: PRC parent company as registered with SAMR
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Because Taiwan is a non-Hague destination, do not apostille; use the Cross-Strait Consular Legalization mechanism exclusively: notarize the articles, transmit them to SEF via the notary association, obtain SEF verification, and attach the verified copy to the incorporation application.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the PRC parent company's main operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed PRC commercial bank holding the parent company's account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the bank officer's signature and bank authority at a PRC notary office, use the provincial notary association to SEF transmission and verification; a Hague Apostille is not valid or accepted in Taiwan; the SEF-verified bank letter must be dated no more than 90 days before submission.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Screen all directors, shareholders, UBOs, authorized signatories, and agents of the WFOE and its PRC parent against PRC and Taiwan domestic AML/CFT lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN sanctions lists, UN Security Council asset-freeze and terrorism resolutions, FATF high-risk jurisdiction statements, and consolidated EU/UK sanctions. Apply fuzzy matching by Chinese, Pinyin, traditional/simplified variants, passport numbers, and aliases. PEPs, their family members and close associates require senior-management approval, documented source of wealth and funds, and enhanced ongoing monitoring for at least five years. Escalate sanctioned-persons hits immediately to the cross-border compliance committee and relevant authorities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System (One-Stop Service for Company and Commercial Registration)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name must be in Traditional Chinese; an English name may be registered only as a supplementary transliteration and cannot be the sole legal name. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) the Chinese company name; (2) the registered English name; (3) the romanized Pinyin or Wade-Giles transliteration; and (4) the abbreviated short title. The Chinese name must contain an industry-specific business identifier and a 'Limited Company' legal ending and must not duplicate or be deceptively similar to existing Taiwan registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving a rejection notice, file a written re-examination with the Department of Commerce, attaching the rejection notice and a revised Traditional Chinese name with a distinctive industry-specific element that removes the cited prohibited or

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act, Articles 5, 6, 18, 98 to 113, 129, 161, 162, 387 and 408; Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals, Articles 4, 7 and 8; Business Tax Act of Taiwan, Articles 28 and 32
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs, Taiwan - Company Registration Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Company (Company Incorporation Registration Application)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital requirement is prescribed under the Taiwan Company Act; however, the paid-in capital must be firmly stated in the Articles of Incorporation, fully subscribed, and fully paid before the company registration filing is made. For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise, the capital amount must be approved by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, and the funds must be remitted from abroad through a designated foreign-exchange bank and verified by a Taiwan-certified public accountant. No blocked escrow account is required, but the remitted capital must remain in a bank account in Taiwan and may not be disbursed for operating expenses until the Company Registration Certificate and Unified Business Number have been issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [CN WFOE LTD] (A Taiwan Limited Company)

WHEREAS the shareholders and incorporators have resolved to organize [CN WFOE LTD] (the "Company") as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise under the Taiwan Company Act, and the directors have been lawfully designated; and

WHEREAS the board is authorized under the Company's Articles of Incorporation and the Investment Approval issued by the Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, to take all necessary actions relating to the formation and governance of the Company;

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors hereby RESOLVES as follows:

1. Ratification of Incorporation and Share Capital Subscription. The incorporation process commenced by the shareholders is hereby ratified, and the subscription to the fully paid-up share capital of the Company in the amount of New Taiwan Dollars [1,000,000], divided into [100,000] shares of par value NT$[10] each, is approved. The Chairperson or General Manager is expressly authorized to collect contribution receipts, to execute share subscription and allotment schedules, and to instruct the certified public accountant to issue the capital verification report required by the competent authority.

2. Banking Authorization. The Company shall establish one or more corporate accounts with [Bank Name], Taiwan Branch, or such other bank as the Chairperson selects. The Chairperson and the General Manager are jointly authorized to open, manage, close and operate the accounts, to sign withdrawal and deposit forms, to execute foreign exchange declarations, and to receive banking correspondence. This authorization is effective until revoked by a written resolution of the board.

3. Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [Address, Taiwan], and the Chairperson is authorized to execute the lease, the landlord's consent, and the occupancy certificate, and to deliver the registered office notice to the Department of Commercial Affairs.

4. Appointment of Officers. [Name of Chairperson] is appointed as Chairperson and statutory representative of the Company; [Name of Director] is appointed as Director; and [Name of General Manager] is appointed as General Manager. Each officer accepts the duties of care, loyalty, and good faith imposed by the Taiwan Company Act and undertakes to cause the Company to file all required statutory returns and maintain proper accounts.

5. Further Authorization. All officers and agents are authorized to execute any additional instruments, to make any declarations, and to pay all fees necessary to obtain the Companies Registration Certificate, the Unified Business Number, tax and labor registrations, and any non-industrial permits applicable to the Company's digital audiovisual post-production services. All acts performed prior to the date of this resolution in connection with the formation are hereby ratified and confirmed.

This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force until amended by a later resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company and Commerce Registration Portal, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating shareholder or its Taiwan-licensed agent shall log into the MOEA One-Stop Company Registration Portal, complete the company name pre-approval application, and designate the future company's English and Chinese trade names. The application must list the principal business scope as ISIC 5912, Motion picture, video and television programme post-production activities, with a commercial description covering automated subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning, dubbing studio, and consulting services. The system and examiner will screen for identical or confusingly similar names and verify that the business scope is permissible for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise. No notarization is required at this stage, but the foreign shareholder's power of attorney must be uploaded. After approval, the name reservation is valid for six months, within which the investor must obtain the required foreign investment approval and continue the formation process.
required_dossiers: Company name pre-approval application form
Draft Articles of Incorporation with Chinese translation
Foreign investor passport or certificate of incorporation
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan agent
Business scope and operation description letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name pre-approval is rejected as identical or confusingly similar, the applicant may submit a revised name reservation within five business days using a change application; alternate names should be submitted to avoid recurrence. There is no formal administrative appeal at the name stage, but the applicant may request a written statement of rejection and resubmit after adding distinctive business identifiers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval by the Investment Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The foreign investor must file, after name reservation, a foreign investment application under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals. The submission must disclose the ultimate beneficial owner, source of inward funds, planned paid-in capital, shareholding percentages, and a three-year business plan. The Investment Commission will review whether the proposed AI subtitle transcription and voice cloning studio is consistent with Taiwan's foreign investment policy and Article 18 restrictions on business scope. If the ultimate beneficial owner is in a specially regulated jurisdiction, supplementary declarations and evidence of lawful source of funds are required. The approval letter sets forth the maximum approved investment amount and the deadline for capital remittance. The certificate must be obtained before remitting capital.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment application form
Investment Approval pre-application ID
Name reservation certificate
Passport or certificate of incorporation with notarized Chinese translation
Bank reference letter
Three-year business plan and projected financials
Certificate of beneficial ownership and anti-money-laundering declaration
Power of attorney for Taiwan agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query or a request for clarification, the investor shall respond through the same electronic platform within 14 days, attaching supplementary evidence; a 14-day extension may be requested. If the application is rejected, the investor may submit an administrative petition to the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days after receipt of the written decision, and may re-file with a revised investment plan if material changes are made.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance, Bank Verification, and CPA Capital Certification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated Foreign Exchange Bank and Certified Public Accountant, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Investment Approval Certificate, the investor shall open a temporary corporate bank account in the future company name with a designated foreign exchange bank. The inward remittance must be made by the approved foreign investor for exactly the amount stated in the approval letter, and the transaction must be accompanied by the required foreign exchange declaration. The bank will issue an inbound remittance record and a foreign exchange declaration certificate. The investor shall deliver the remittance certificates to a Taiwan-certified public accountant, who will review the credit entries and issue a statutory capital verification report. This report is a mandatory attachment to the incorporation registration and is accepted by the registry as evidence of fully paid capital. The funds remain restricted in the company account and cannot be disbursed for operating expenses until the Company Registration Certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Investment Approval Certificate
Corporate account opening application and seal card
Bank wire confirmation and foreign exchange declaration forms
CPA capital verification report
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Shareholder ledger with contribution amounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remitted amount differs from the approved investment amount, the investor must return or supplement the funds before CPA certification, or apply for a change to the investment approval with the Investment Commission. If the bank rejects the account opening due to beneficial ownership issues, the investor shall provide an enhanced corporate ownership structure chart and a source-of-funds statement, and the matter may be resolved within 10 days by re-presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration with the Department of Commercial Affairs
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fifteen days after the effective date of incorporation, the statutory representative must submit the Company Incorporation Registration Application to the Department of Commercial Affairs. The application must include the name reservation approval, the Investment Approval Certificate, the adopted Articles of Incorporation, the CPA capital verification report, the registered office lease or occupancy consent, and the written consent of the directors and supervisors to act as such. The representative shall also submit the company seal registration card and pay the incorporation registration fee. The authority will verify that the company name, paid-in capital, business scope, and statutory representatives comply with the Taiwan Company Act. Upon approval, the Department issues the Company Registration Certificate and assigns the Unified Business Number, which also functions as the tax identification number.
required_dossiers: Company incorporation registration application
Name reservation approval certificate
Foreign investment approval certificate
Articles of Incorporation in Chinese
CPA capital verification report
Consent letters of directors and supervisors
Registered office consent with lease certificate
Passport and ID copies with Chinese name declarations
Power of attorney and notarized seals
Company seal and uniform invoice seal card
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a deficiency notice, the applicant has 15 days from receipt to cure the omissions, and a 30-day extension may be requested if authority certificates are delayed. If the 15-day registration window is missed, the applicant may file late with the registry and pay any applicable late charge; if the application is formally rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Business Registration, Uniform Invoicing, and Labor Operational Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance, Taiwan and local Labor Insurance and Health Insurance Administration units
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Company Registration Certificate is granted, the WFOE must complete business tax registration with the local National Taxation Bureau under the Business Tax Act. The tax authority will record the company address, legal representative, and business scope, and will approve the company as a Uniform Invoice issuer. The company must also register as a withholding agent for employee income tax and as an employer for labor insurance, health insurance, and labor pension contributions. Because ISIC 5912 digital post-production does not require a manufacturing operating license, the remaining formalities are standard office registrations: submission of the registered address lease, landlord consent, bank account verification, and responsible-person identification. The company should also establish mandatory work rules if it employs more than 30 workers, and appoint a workplace safety and health officer as required for office environments under the Occupational Safety and Health Act of Taiwan.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Company seal and uniform invoice seal
Business Registration Application Form
Registered office lease and landlord consent
Responsible person photo ID and domicile proof
Articles of Incorporation and board resolution
Bank account verification certificate
Employee roster and labor and health insurance enrolment forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax bureau queries the application, the company should file a supplemental statement with lease and rental withholding certificates within 10 days. Any delay in uniform invoice approval can be remedied by requesting provisional invoice allocation; labor registration corrections can be filed electronically within 7 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the competent industrial authority for factories and plants in Taiwan would be the Ministry of Economic Affairs Administration for Industrial Development, but no factory registration is required because the WFOE conducts no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operations.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit is prescribed for ISIC 5912 post-production subtitling and AI voice-cloning services; the entity operates as a digital audiovisual post-production studio under its Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Invoice Registration only.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - the Environmental Protection Administration of Taiwan would be the responsible agency for category-listed industrial projects, but this is an office-based digital service with no physical project installation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - No category-listed project under the Taiwan Environmental Impact Assessment Act; no Full EIA Report or Environmental Registration is required for an office-based AI audiovisual post-production and voice simulation studio.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, point-source air emissions, VOC discharge, or hazardous waste generation. Domestic sewage from office washrooms is discharged to the municipal sewer under local sewer authority standards, and any electronic waste must be recycled through a licensed recycler under the Taiwan Waste Disposal Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as an industrial civil-defense permit; however, the office premises must obtain the standard fire safety compliance inspection and equipment certification from the local Fire Bureau under the Fire Services Act, and the employer must file an occupational safety and health self-inspection and designate a health and safety officer if worker thresholds under the Occupational Safety and Health Act of Taiwan are exceeded.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); online portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (ETB) at www.chinatax.gov.cn
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: The WFOE is incorporated under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), which issues a business license containing a Unified Social Credit Code (USCC); the USCC is the statutory TIN and is automatically transmitted to the STA through the integrated multi-license reform data-sharing system. Step 2: Within 30 days of incorporation, the WFOE's legal representative and financial officer must activate the national Electronic Tax Bureau (ETB) account using real-name authentication (e-identification). Step 3: In the ETB, complete the post-registration tax filing confirmation by verifying tax types (Corporate Income Tax, VAT, stamp duty, urban maintenance and construction tax, individual income tax withholding), selecting the VAT taxpayer status, and confirming the tax collection period. Step 4: Apply for the All-Digital Electronic Invoice quota and authorize the VAT electronic invoice platform. Step 5: A foreign non-resident investor that will derive China-source income must either register directly via the STA's non-resident taxpayer workflow or be enrolled as a withholding-tax payer through the WFOE as the withholding agent. Failure to complete ETB activation within 30 days may trigger late-registration penalties under the Tax Collection and Administration Law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box pass-through election is available under China's CIT regime; a WFOE is always an entity-level taxpayer. The only relevant election is VAT status: a taxpayer may elect simplified small-scale treatment until annual taxable turnover exceeds 5,000,000 CNY, after which general VAT taxpayer registration is compulsory. Anti-hybrid rules under CIT Law Article 46 and relevant MOF/STA circulars disallow interest deductions for hybrid mismatch arrangements; no protective election exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 5,000,000 CNY annual taxable turnover (mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration boundary; VAT registration itself is due within 30 days of incorporation for all entities irrespective of turnover)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Since the nationwide rollout of the All-Digital Electronic Invoice (e-invoice) system, all VAT invoices must be created through the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform. Each e-invoice carries a unique digital invoice code, an anti-counterfeit QR code, and a digital stamp generated in real time by the Golden Tax Phase IV (GTP IV) system. e-invoice data is cleared through the STA cloud before release to the recipient; no invoice can be issued offline except legacy registered paper invoices. Enterprises connect their billing systems via the STA's authorized API or the web interface, and every issuance is reported transactionally to enable automatic cross-checking of VAT credits.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the STA's Cross-border Taxable Services Zero-Rate and Exemption Administration Measures, an AI subtitle transcription and voice cloning studio may claim a 0% VAT export rate by proving: (a) the service is supplied to a customer resident outside China (including Taiwan); (b) the service is consumed wholly outside the customs territory of China; (c) consideration is received in foreign exchange or in RMB settled from an overseas bank; and (d) the services fall within the zero-rated catalogue for modern services (broadcasting, film and audio-video production and post-production services). The WFOE must file a zero-rate declaration in the export tax rebate system and retain contemporaneous evidence for audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) - required only when physical media, master discs, or encoded hardware are separately declared; not applicable to pure digital delivery.
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill - required only for tangible exports; digital services rely on electronic delivery receipts and log files.
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange receipt record issued by a Chinese-designated settlement bank, evidencing repatriation of export proceeds in the agreed currency.
Export Service Contract executed between the WFOE and the offshore customer, specifying the AI subtitle transcription/dubbing services, fees, currency, and delivery terms.
All-Digital Electronic Invoice (e-invoice) issued through the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform indicating the 0% VAT zero-rate annotation.

Offshore Consumption Declaration signed by the WFOE (and if required, a beneficial owner certificate from the customer's tax authority) confirming the service is provided and consumed entirely outside China.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Where zero-rating is claimed on fabricated or non-qualifying services, the STA will disallow the zero-rate, claw back the uncollected VAT, and charge a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% from the date the tax became due. A tax penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax may be imposed under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law. Fraudulent export rebate claims may trigger unlimited retrospective reassessment, criminal liability under Article 201 of the Criminal Law, and inclusion on the Tax Dishonesty Blacklist, suspending export tax incentives and restricting the legal representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and its State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under China's current foreign exchange administration framework, the renminbi is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods, services, and profit remittances, subject to a principle of genuine documentation verification. Capital account items, such as direct investment, cross-border debt, and securities investment, remain regulated and require prior approval, filing, or registration with SAFE. For a wholly foreign-owned enterprise (WFOE), registered capital must be remitted through a foreign exchange capital account and can be converted into RMB for business use under the capital account settlement guidelines, with strict tracking and payment verification. Profit remittance to overseas parents requires an audited financial statement, proof of tax payment, and a resolution on dividend distribution; funds must pass through a bank account and be settled under the current account regime. Although the SAFE has removed the mandatory export surrender requirement, export proceeds must be repatriated and brought onshore within the statutory period. The de facto convertibility is therefore high for current account operations but constrained for capital account flows, and any perceived arbitrage or round-tripping is scrutinized intensively. This dual-track regime necessitates meticulous transactional documentation and compliance with the 'principle of actual need'. Additionally, the AI subtitle and voice-cloning business, classified under ISIC 5912, may involve cross-border data flows and intellectual property licensing, which are subject to separate PBOC and Cybersecurity Administration oversight, adding both risk and documentary complexity to any currency conversion or repatriation exercise.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: As of the current SAFE rules, there is no mandatory surrender ratio for export proceeds. Exporters must repatriate all foreign exchange receipts from exports to mainland China within 30 days, or within 90 days if the foreign trade contract stipulates a longer settlement period, and must complete the export collection verification through the Trade in Goods Monitoring System. The exporter may choose to keep the funds in a foreign currency current account or convert them into RMB at the prevailing spot rate. For service trade income, such as AI subtitle production and voice-cloning licensing, similar rules apply: the invoice must be matched against the service transaction and settled through the bank, with full documentation retained for five years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Escrow) and Basic Settlement Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Deposit Account plus Foreign Exchange Current Account for Trade Settlements
Foreign Exchange Current Account and Payment Facilitation Account for Cross-Border Services
Foreign Exchange Settlement Account and RMB Disbursement Sub-Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Stripe and Wise are not licensed payment institutions in mainland China and cannot directly open accounts or clear transactions for a WFOE. For a Chinese incorporated entity, any attempt to use these offshore EMIs to originate or receive payments would violate PBOC regulations on cross-border payment services and SAFE rules on foreign exchange settlement. The only permissible route for high-volume, compliant cross-border collection and disbursement is through licensed domestic banks using SWIFT or its Chinese equivalent (CIPS). Therefore, the viability of fintech EMIs for this WFOE is low, and institutions such as Stripe or Wise should be used solely by the offshore parent or affiliated entities, never by the mainland entity itself. The financial superintendent must ensure that all business revenue is received via the WFOE's bank-approved invoices and bank transfer channels, otherwise the entity faces real-time anomalous transaction monitoring and potential freezing of accounts.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law and PBOC Account Opening Circularity, the legal representative and at least one authorized director/beneficial owner must appear physically at the bank branch for a face-to-face interview and biometric verification during the initial KYC onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognized by any Tier-1 Chinese commercial bank; however, in exceptional cases where the legal representative is outside mainland China, a notarized power of attorney executed with the Chinese embassy or consulate may be presented, and a senior bank compliance officer may conduct a remote video interview, but final discretion remains with the bank's head office compliance committee. For this WFOE, the statutory director (whether based in Taiwan or elsewhere) must make an in-person visit to the chosen bank's corporate banking center before any account is activated, and all UBOs holding 25% or more of the equity must submit original identification documents and a clean-source-of-funds declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership complexity arising from a Taiwan-based parent or group shareholders with cross-strait capital structures.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide up-to-date corporate registry extracts of the entire holding chain, a notarized trust deed and declaration of beneficial owner(s) in English and Chinese, audited financial statements of the ultimate parent for the last two years, a board resolution assigning the WFOE's capital commitment, and a written description of the source of wealth and source of funds for each shareholder holding more than 10% equity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: AI-related intellectual property and royalty payments to overseas licensors that may be misclassified as service fees, creating profit-shifting risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a detailed IP licensing agreement with clear deliverables and usage limitations, invoices, proof of actual delivery (e.g., cloud logs, project updates), tax withholding certificates for royalty payments to non-residents, and a SAFE trade-service filing confirming the transaction's authenticity and purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency, small-value inbound proceeds from foreign platforms inconsistent with the declared business size of the entity, typical of micro-subscription or task-based AI work.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a platform activity report from the foreign publishing or streaming platform, customer contracts, an explanation of the unit pricing for subtitle/voice services, an audit trail reconciling each inbound payment to a corresponding service order, and a bank reference letter from the platform's settlement bank; additionally, implement an internal policy to generate a monthly reconciliation pack for the bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to sanctioned or restricted end-users due to the AI voice-cloning outputs, which might inadvertently support content distribution in embargoed jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a comprehensive export-control compliance manual, proof of screening of all clients and counterparties against OFAC, UN, and PRC sanctions lists using a certified screening tool, end-user certificates from all significant clients, and a signed undertaking that no services are rendered to entities in sanctioned regions, along with an internal AML compliance calendar.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection for the WFOE must be routed through a designated foreign exchange capital account opened at an approved domestic bank (e.g., BOC or ICBC). The remittance from the Taiwan investor must be denominated in USD or TWD (converted at the bank's spot rate) and must carry the payment purpose code '622' (Investment of Foreign-Funded Enterprises). Upon arrival, the bank will issue an FDI Business Registration Certificate and the entity must complete capital verification through a certified public accountant within a prescribed timeframe. The capital may then be converted into RMB under the 'Whole Amount Early Settlement of Foreign Exchange Capital' scheme, but every conversion must be accompanied by a written declaration of the intended use, and the RMB funds must be deposited into a Disbursement Sub-Account from which only genuine domestic operating expenses can be paid. Any misuse or diversion of these funds to offshore accounts triggers severe penalties.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For outbound service and trade payments, the WFOE may use standard SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for supplier invoices, royalty payments, and consulting fees, provided the bank receives a trade background document package (contract, commercial invoice, tax papers, and SAFE reporting). For larger or asset-protected transactions, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (at sight or usance) issued by the WFOE's bank in favor of the overseas beneficiary is admissible; alternatively, Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A) can be used for physical goods-related transactions. Since the business scope is digital services, MT103 with a clear service description and a valid underlying contract is the most efficient rail. All foreign exchange purchases must be done at the bank manually, and the bank will send the FX payment instruction to the overseas clearing system using SWIFT or CIPS depending on the counterparty's location; for Taiwanese counterparties, the transaction may be routed directly to Taiwan's CNAPS or via SWIFT with a standard MT202 for bank-to-bank covers.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forward Contracts up to 12 months, requiring a real underlying current or capital account transaction with confirmation of hedging capacity and SAFE filing
FX Swaps (spot against forward) for managing short-term liquidity mismatches, executed only with a domestic appointed bank under the real needs test

Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for long-term foreign currency debt servicing, permitted with prior SAFE registration and only for documented exposures; onshore NDFs are strictly prohibited, but offshore non-deliverable forwards can be used by the parent entity outside China as a parallel hedge

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end, covering prior-year operations, shareholding structure, and audit opinion
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Persistent non-filing may void the foreign investment approval, trigger administrative fines, and cause the Investment Commission to compel divestment or deregistration; the company may also lose access to approved capital remittance privileges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (domicile tax office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 May following the close of the calendar fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 10% of unpaid tax if filed within 10 days after the due date and 20% if filed later; overdue tax accrues monthly interest, and continued non-payment can trigger provisional attachment of assets and exit restriction on responsible officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and Audited or Board-Approved Financial Statements filed after the Annual General Meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Company Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held no later than 30 June; the financial statements and business report must be filed with MOEA within 15 days after AGM approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The responsible persons may be fined between NT$20,000 and NT$100,000 (approximately US$650 to US$3,250); repeated failure to file may lead to administrative revocation and forced dissolution by MOEA.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation of Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) and Event-Driven UBO Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) - Central Company Registration and UBO Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 15 days after any change in beneficial ownership or covering shareholding transfer; this office also performs an annual KYC reconciliation by 31 May of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or false filing carries fines of NT$10,000 to NT$100,000 (approximately US$325 to US$3,250) per event, with repeated breaches exposed to escalated administrative penalties and ultimately strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Payroll and Withholding Tax Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance (tax collection office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of the year following the withholding calendar year, with employee copies furnished by the same date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file withholding statements triggers a fine of NT$1,500 to NT$15,000 (approximately US$48 to US$480) for each violation; repeated or egregious failures may result in enhanced fines, back-tax assessment, and criminal referral.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent CPA audit is legally required where the Taiwan company: (i) is a public company making a public offering; (ii) has paid-in capital of NT$30 million or more (approximately US$1.0 million); (iii) has prior-year net operating revenue of NT$100 million or more (approximately US$3.3 million); (iv) employed 100 or more staff members; (v) is a financial, insurance, trust, securities, or other regulated enterprise designated by the Financial Supervisory Commission; or (vi) has obtained Investment Commission approval conditioned on audited financial statements. These thresholds are assessed under Article 20 of the Company Act and the MOEA CPA audit threshold regulations, using balance-sheet, turnover, and headcount measurements on the legal entity statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies must apply International Financial Reporting Standards as endorsed in Taiwan (T-IFRS). Non-public SMEs may apply the Business Entity Financial Reporting Regulations and the SME Financial Accounting Standards (SME-GAAP), or electively adopt full T-IFRS. All statutory financial statements must comply with the Commercial Accounting Act and Company Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Although some global AML frameworks impose a 30-day reporting window, Taiwan Company Act Article 22-1 imposes a stricter 15-day filing window for any change in ultimate beneficial ownership. This office therefore executes an annual cycle: (1) a KYC refresh no later than 31 March; (2) final UBO register and MOEA-portal reconciliation by 31 May alongside the income tax return; and (3) an event-driven filing within 15 calendar days of every shareholding transfer or control change.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges, Mortgages, and Secured Liens
Statutory Minute Book (shareholders and directors resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$400 to US$1,200 per year for a registered office and corporate secretarial agent in Taipei; US$1,200 to US$3,500 for a physical serviced office with mail handling
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 to US$7,500 for a threshold-triggered statutory audit of a low-risk AI post-production SME; voluntary audit or agreed-upon procedures typically cost US$1,800 to US$4,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard Enterprise Income Tax (EIT) rate under PRC EIT Law Article 4; non-resident enterprise passive income is charged at 20% and effectively reduced to 10% for outbound dividends, interest and royalties under EIT Implementation Regulation Article 91. The WFOE, as a Chinese tax resident, is taxed on worldwide income at 25% unless a preferential rate applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified small low-profit enterprise concession (taxable income up to RMB 3 million, employees up to 300, total assets up to RMB 50 million) yields an effective 5% CIT rate for tax years 2023 through 2027 by applying a 75% reduction to the 20% reduced rate. Certified High and New Technology Enterprise (HNTE) rate of 15% is available to the AI subtitle and voice-technology entity if R&D expenditure ratios and technology scope tests are met, with loss carryforward extended to 10 years. An additional 100% super-deduction applies to qualifying R&D expenses, and certified software enterprises may reach a 10% rate on qualifying software-related income. No statutory tax holiday applies to ordinary WFOE post-production service revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return Form A (中华人民共和国企业所得税年度纳税申报表 A类), main form code A100000, together with the A000000 basic information form, income and expense schedules (A101010, A102010, A104000), tax adjustment schedule (A105000), incentive schedules (A107010-A107042), foreign tax credit schedule (A108000) and, where related-party transactions exist, the annual related-party transaction reporting forms (G100000-G114000 series) under SAT Announcement No. 42/2016. Filing is performed electronically through the State Taxation Administration electronic tax bureau portal (全国统一电子税务局).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional CIT payments (预缴) due within 15 days after each quarter-end, followed by an annual final settlement and reconciliation (汇算清缴) covering the calendar year ended 31 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly instalments: due by 15 April, 15 July, 15 October and 15 January (for the fourth quarter). Annual reconciliation return and final balance payment: due by 31 May of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, unified social credit code, industry classification (ISIC 5912 equivalent), tax collection method, registered capital, shareholder structure and WFOE foreign-investment registration status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declare the Taiwan-origin ultimate beneficial owner and 100% foreign-owned capital structure; confirm the entity is taxed as a resident enterprise on worldwide income; the form must match the Foreign Investment Filing System (FDI/Outbound investment registration) data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating revenue including AI subtitle licensing, dubbing service fees, subscription and post-production income; cost of services; taxes and surcharges; selling, general and administrative expenses; financial expenses; impairment provisions; investment gains; operating profit; non-operating income and expenses; total accounting profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Recognise all revenue settled through Stripe, Wise and any offshore gateways on an accrual basis; cross-border service fees must be supported by contracts and time-clock or deliverable evidence; unreported foreign revenue detected during tax authority data exchange will be treated as concealment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: A100000 Lines 14-21 Taxable Income and Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment increases and decreases (including thin capitalisation disallowances, transfer pricing adjustments, non-deductible entertainment and advertising expenses, depreciation differences), prior-year loss carryforward offset, taxable income, tentative tax at 25%, incentive deductions, final tax payable and balance due for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the Taiwanese shareholder licenses AI model training corpora or trademark rights to the WFOE, verify arm's-length royalty rates and furnish contemporaneous benchmarking with the annual filing; enter the adjusted taxable income consistently with the G100000 series.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income: revenue timing differences, deductible expense limits (business entertainment capped at 60% and 0.5% of revenue; advertising at 15% of revenue), thin capitalisation interest disallowance, transfer pricing adjustments and unrecognised related-party expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany service fees from Taiwan parent must satisfy the beneficial ownership and substance test; a Taiwanese parent invoice without actual delivery of services is non-deductible and recharacterised as a disguised dividend subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: G100000 Related Party Transaction Annual Report
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of related-party relationships and transaction categories: tangible property, intangible property licensing, service transactions and financing with the Taiwan parent and sister companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory whenever any related-party transaction exists, including a deemed service arrangement for management oversight from Taiwan; thresholds trigger mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; omit the report at the peril of a special tax investigation adjustment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fixed penalty of RMB 2,000, or RMB 2,000-10,000 in serious cases, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid tax. Underreporting or failure to pay: additional tax plus a fine of 50%-500% of the shortfall. Responsible persons and the legal representative are exposed to exit-control enforcement for unpaid tax, public credit downgrade, and criminal liability where evasion exceeds the Criminal Law Article 201 thresholds.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on the gross amount of dividends distributed by the Chinese WFOE to its Taiwan shareholder. The 10% is the domestic statutory gross-basis withholding tax for non-resident enterprises without a permanent establishment in China; because the Cross-Strait Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement has been signed but has not entered into force, no treaty reduction is currently available. The WFOE must withhold at the time of the shareholder resolution and remit the WHT to the tax authority by the 15th day of the month following the payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For jurisdictions with an effective tax treaty or tax arrangement, treaty benefits are invoked under SAT Announcement No. 35/2019 by the non-resident beneficial owner, through a written self-assessment, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence jurisdiction authority, and evidence of beneficial ownership and substantive business operations. The withholding agent files the reduced-rate return and retains the treaty package; the tax authority may deny or re-assess benefits if the residence certificate is defective, the holding structure fails the 25% participation test, or the owner is a shell without substantive activities. The procedure is inapplicable to the Taiwan shareholder while the Cross-Strait agreement remains non-effective.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory gross-base WHT for non-resident enterprises is 10% for Chinese-source interest and 10% for Chinese-source royalties. Royalties paid by the WFOE to the Taiwan parent for AI model training data, software copyrights or trademark licences are therefore subject to 10% WHT, and interest on shareholder loans is subject to 10% WHT subject to thin capitalisation limits. Where an effective DTA exists with another jurisdiction, treaty rates commonly range from 5% to 10% for royalties and 5% to 10% for interest; for Taiwan no treaty relief applies.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB. The annual related-party transaction report (G-series) is mandatory for any related-party transaction. Local File (同期资料-本地文档) is required where tangible-property related-party transactions exceed RMB 200 million in a tax year, intangible-property or service-related transactions exceed RMB 40 million, or financial-asset related-party transactions exceed RMB 100 million. Master File (主体文档) is required where aggregate annual related-party transactions exceed RMB 1 billion. Same-period documentation must be completed by 31 May of the following year and delivered to the tax authority within 20 working days of a formal request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not apply the UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations, but economic substance operates through the EIT Law Article 47 general anti-abuse rule, the reasonable-commercial-purpose principle, the beneficial-ownership test in treaty claims, and the anti-round-tripping declaration under SAFE/MOFCOM rules. A Taiwan-funded WFOE with only nominal staff, shared office space, no local decision-making and no control over its AI development contracts is exposed to recharacterisation as a shell/principal vehicle; the tax authority can attribute profits to the substantive owner, deny royalty deductions, reject treaty filings and re-classify undocumented flows as dividends. For the AI subtitle and voice-cloning studio, substantive continuity must be evidenced through local editing hardware, data-security infrastructure, employment contracts of subtitle engineers, contractual assumption of commercial risk and ownership of developed IP on the WFOE side.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion through False Invoicing and Fabricated Costs
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing or issuing fake VAT invoices to inflate production costs, fabricating AI render-farm rental contracts, or booking personal expenses of Taiwanese shareholders as WFOE costs so as to conceal taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional CIT and VAT collection with daily 0.05% surcharge; fine of 50%-500% of the unpaid tax under Tax Administration Law Article 63; false-invoice conduct falls within Criminal Law Article 205, punishable by fines and imprisonment of the entity's responsible personnel (maximum life imprisonment in aggravated cases).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative, financial officer and directly responsible managers face criminal arrest, personal fines, disqualification from management positions and exit bans while tax debts are outstanding; the corporate veil is not pierced automatically but the responsible-person liability rule exposes directors to personal restitution for fraudulent bookkeeping.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation with Taiwan Parent IP
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging zero or artificially low royalties to the Taiwanese parent for AI subtitle engine use, making non-arm's-length service payments to Taiwan without delivery evidence, or stripping profits through excessive group management fees while failing to prepare Local File and Master File.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Special tax re-assessment under EIT Law Articles 41-48 with profit uplift, interest computed from the year of non-payment at the benchmark lending rate plus 5 percentage points, a 10-year look-back period for special tax auditing, and fines under the Tax Administration Law for failure to provide same-period documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly signed the manipulative contracts may be held jointly responsible for the supplementary tax and interest where the arrangement is found to be an evasion scheme; criminal tax evasion liability attaches where the adjusted unpaid tax exceeds the Criminal Law thresholds; travel restrictions may be imposed during the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Disguised Dividends and Failure to Withhold on Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends to the Taiwan shareholder without withholding the 10% WHT, or bypassing the dividend procedure by making loans, shareholder expense payments or royalty overcharges that are in substance profit distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Tax Administration Law Article 69, the WFOE as withholding agent is fined 50%-300% of the unwithheld tax, and the beneficiary is pursued for the unpaid WHT plus daily late surcharge; recharacterised distributions trigger additional thin capitalisation and GAAR adjustments under EIT Law Article 47.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The financial director and legal representative who approved undisclosed distributions are personally liable for the fine and may be subject to exit-control enforcement; intentional non-withholding is treated as tax evasion by the entity and its responsible persons, carrying imprisonment up to seven years and criminal fines.
